title: How much flour will make six rotis?
description: One quarter of a kilogram of flour makes twelve rotis. The flour for one roti comes first, by sharing the quarter among twelve rotis with the reciprocal, and then the flour for six rotis is found by multiplying.
teaching_notes: One idea: find the amount for one roti by dividing, then multiply by the number of rotis wanted. Watch for students who forget to go through one roti and guess a fraction of the quarter.

source: Figure it Out (problems with fractions): if 1/4 kg of flour is used to make 12 rotis, how much flour is used to make 6 rotis?
video_script.why: A learner shares a fraction among many pieces, then takes several of them.
video_script.substitution: the book's own flour for twelve rotis, asked for six rotis
video_script.anchor: twelve rotis made from one quarter of a kilogram of flour
video_script.payoff_line: Six rotis use one eighth of a kilogram of flour.
video_script.fraction_reading: one quarter, one forty eighth, one eighth
video_script.design: Twelve rotis in a row under one quarter kilogram; the working band finds one roti first, then six.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; twelve rotis in a row beside a bag marked one quarter kilogram of flour

marks.flour: the bag with one quarter kilogram appears
marks.rotis: twelve rotis appear in a row
marks.ask: six of the rotis light up

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about making rotis.
<bookmark mark='flour'/>One quarter of a kilogram of flour is used to make twelve rotis.
<bookmark mark='rotis'/>The flour is shared equally among the twelve rotis.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much flour is used to make six rotis?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits beside the rotis

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the quarter kilogram split into twelve equal parts, one under each roti

marks.split: the flour splits into twelve equal parts
marks.one: one part lights up under one roti

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Each roti gets the same share of the flour.
<bookmark mark='one'/>If we know the flour for one roti, we can find it for any number of rotis.
<bookmark mark='recip'/>The reciprocal of twelve is one twelfth.
Dividing by twelve is multiplying by one twelfth.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1/4 kg of flour for 12 rotis

marks.given: the flour and the number of rotis are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one quarter of a kilogram of flour makes twelve rotis.

marks.find: the words flour for six rotis are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the flour used for six rotis.

marks.one: one quarter divided by twelve is written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, the flour is shared among twelve rotis.
The flour for one roti is one quarter divided by twelve.

marks.recip: one twelfth replaces twelve and the sign turns to times
marks.mult: the numerators and the denominators are multiplied

narration: <bookmark mark='recip'/>Step two, multiply by the reciprocal of twelve, as in the method of your book.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>One times one over four times twelve is one forty eighth of a kilogram for one roti.

marks.six: six times one forty eighth is written

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step three, six rotis use six times the flour of one roti, six times one forty eighth.

marks.check: twelve times one forty eighth is written and matches one quarter

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the share for one roti. Twelve rotis of one forty eighth each give back one quarter.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Six rotis use one eighth of a kilogram of flour.
Six rotis are half of twelve rotis, and one eighth is half of one quarter.
